hypothesis: Embedding automated regulatory compliance checks (rule-based + ML) and redaction into the localization pipeline, both pre- and post-localization, will (a) significantly increase the detection rate of compliance-relevant issues and (b) reduce residual high-severity violations in finalized localized content, without increasing average end-to-end pipeline latency by more than 20% relative to a baseline pipeline that relies on manual, end-of-process legal review only.

baseline.description: Baseline AI localization pipeline with manual, end-of-process legal review only and minimal technical compliance controls.
workflow_stages: ingestion: content (e.g., pharma IFU, financial disclosure) pulled from sample CMS/TMS export
localization: MT/LLM-based translation with terminology support from Chapter 5 baseline
export: localized artifacts exported for human linguistic review and single consolidated legal review at the end
legal-review: manual legal/compliance review using a static checklist; corrections applied ad hoc outside the automated pipeline

compliance_controls.in_pipeline: no automated redaction; no automated compliance screening; no controlled-vocabulary enforcement beyond generic glossary checks
compliance_controls.post_localization: single manual legal/compliance review relying on human spotting of issues; no structured machine support

data_handling.pii_phr: PII/PHI present in some workloads is not automatically redacted before MT/LLM calls; assumes a trusted vendor and BAA/DPA but no technical enforcement
data_handling.logging: minimal operational logs only (errors, durations); no structured compliance evidence logs

human_in_the_loop.linguistic_review: optional linguistic review for all workloads, focused on language quality, not structured compliance criteria
human_in_the_loop.legal_review: mandatory manual review for high-risk content only (pharma and finance workloads); medium-risk content may skip legal review in baseline configuration

treatment.description: Enhanced AI localization pipeline with automated rule-based and ML-driven compliance checks, redaction/anonymization, controlled vocabularies, and structured audit logging integrated pre- and post-localization.
workflow_stages: ingestion: same as baseline; content pulled from identical sources and normalized
pre-screening: automated PII/PHI detection + redaction/anonymization; high-risk topics flagged using ML classifier; jurisdiction tagging

pre-localization-compliance-checks: rule-based checks on source content against jurisdiction-specific policies (e.g., forbidden phrases, missing mandatory disclosures); controlled-vocabulary enforcement for regulated terms
localization: MT/LLM-based translation with same engines as baseline; MT prompts enriched with compliance constraints (e.g., "use approved terms", "do not add unapproved claims")

post-localization-compliance-checks: rule-based + ML checks on localized content (forbidden claims, risk wording, presence/absence of mandated statements, PII leakage, high-risk entities); terminological compliance verification vs. approved term lists
audit-logging: structured, append-only logs of every compliance rule evaluation, ML model score, redaction operation, and human override with timestamps and content hashes

human-review: risk-based routing: (a) compliance-flagged items must go through legal review; (b) non-flagged but high-risk asset types get sample-based legal review; (c) low-risk items may be auto-approved if passing all checks
legal-signoff: legal reviewers work from a compliance console-like view summarizing detected and resolved issues; approval is logged with reviewer ID and version hash

pre_localization.pii_redaction: Automatic masking/replacement of PII/PHI using a rule-based + ML NER stack before sending text to external MT/LLM services; reversible mapping held in a secure local store if business needs require de-anonymization.
pre_localization.source_content_checks: Regex- and rule-based checks for known regulatory clauses (e.g., presence of EMA/FDA-mandated statements; FINRA/SEC disclaimers); ML topic/risk classifier to flag content as pharma-safety, financial-promo, generic, etc.
pre_localization.controlled_vocab_source: Validation that certain regulated source phrases map to an approved set of source-language terms (e.g., medical indications, risk categories).

post_localization.target_compliance_rules: Language-specific rule sets enforcing: (a) no unapproved therapeutic claims, (b) required risk disclosures present, (c) no prohibited financial promises, (d) labels/warnings preserved.
post_localization.terminology_enforcement: Check that key regulated terms in the target text use approved localized equivalents from controlled vocabularies; log any deviations with suggested fixes.
post_localization.residual_pii_detection: Run PII detector on target text to ensure redaction is still in effect and no PII/PHI leaked via model hallucination.

auditability.logging: All compliance checks (rule and ML) emit structured JSON entries including content_id, version, rule_id/model_id, input hash, output, decision (pass/fail/uncertain), severity, and remediation_action.
auditability.evidence_generation: For each localized artifact, a machine-readable 'compliance dossier' is produced aggregating checks, redactions, reviewer actions, and approvals; hashes allow verifying content integrity.
auditability.replayability: Deterministic seeds for ML inference (where supported) and pinned model versions ensure reproducible re-runs of checks on the same content snapshot.

workloads.description: Pharmaceutical Instructions for Use (IFU), patient leaflets, and safety communications in English localized into Spanish (es-ES) and German (de-DE).
regulatory_context: EU EMA medicinal product information requirements
FDA guidance on prescription drug labeling (for US-origin text as a proxy)
Data protection where patient stories are present (GDPR/PHI-like scenarios)

characteristics.pii_presence: medium (patient names, dates, case IDs present in subset)
characteristics.compliance_anchors: mandatory risk statements, contraindications, dosage sections, black-box warnings

workloads.description: Retail investment product summaries and marketing disclosures in English localized into French (fr-FR) and German (de-DE).
regulatory_context: Local advertising and marketing rules for financial products
Data protection where customer scenarios may include PII

characteristics.pii_presence: low to medium (names in testimonials or scenarios)
characteristics.compliance_anchors: capital-at-risk statements, past-performance disclaimers, non-guarantee clauses

workloads.description: Customer support tickets with embedded PII/PHI (names, email addresses, account numbers, health-related info) in English localized into Spanish (es-ES).
regulatory_context: HIPAA-like PHI privacy constraints where applicable
Corporate internal privacy policy for cross-border processing

characteristics.compliance_anchors: complete removal or pseudonymization of PII/PHI in content sent to external vendors

workloads.description: Generic low-risk marketing web copy (e.g., product features descriptions) in English localized into French (fr-FR). Used to measure false positive rate and latency impact.
regulatory_context: Standard advertising guidelines without sector-specific rules

characteristics.compliance_anchors: no specific mandated clauses; mainly brand and fairness constraints

controls.randomization: For each workload, each document is randomly assigned to baseline or treatment pipeline using a fixed random seed; assignments are stratified by document type and risk markers so both arms contain comparable distributions of high-risk sections, PII density, and length.
controls.content_versioning: Input documents are stored as immutable, versioned artifacts (e.g., Git LFS or content-addressed storage) so baseline and treatment operate on identical inputs per-stratum, even if assignment differs.
controls.translation_engine: The same MT/LLM model versions, configs, and terminology resources are used in baseline and treatment; only compliance-specific stages differ.
controls.environment: Both pipelines run in identical container images with pinned dependencies and identical hardware/VM specs.
controls.blinded_annotation: Human legal/compliance annotators assessing residual violations see only the final localized text and a random anonymized document ID; they are blinded to whether content came from baseline or treatment pipeline.
controls.order_effects: For any document that needs human annotation, annotators do not see both baseline and treatment versions of the same document; documents are partitioned between annotators to avoid recall bias.
controls.jurisdictional_rules: Rule sets are frozen before the experiment and versioned; no mid-run rule adjustments are allowed. Any necessary corrections result in a new experiment_id.

metrics.name: detected_compliance_issues_per_1k_tokens
metrics.description: Number of compliance-relevant issues flagged automatically (rule-based + ML) per 1,000 tokens of source or target text, stratified by severity and workload.

metrics.name: residual_high_severity_violations_rate
metrics.description: Average count of confirmed high-severity regulatory violations per document remaining after pipeline completion and human legal review, as assessed by blinded expert annotators using a standardized rubric.

metrics.name: false_positive_issue_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of automatically flagged issues that human legal/compliance reviewers label as 'not actually a violation nor risk'.

metrics.name: pii_leakage_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of documents containing any unredacted PII/PHI in the content actually sent to external MT/LLM services (pre-localization leak) and in final localized outputs (post-localization leak).

metrics.name: average_pipeline_latency
metrics.description: Average end-to-end processing time from ingestion to ready-for-legal-review output for each document.

metrics.name: legal_review_time_per_document
metrics.description: Average human legal/compliance review time per document, captured via UI event logs or manual time tracking.

metrics.name: legal_escalation_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of documents escalated by legal/compliance reviewers for further investigation or rework after initial review.

metrics.name: terminology_compliance_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of required regulated terms in the target language that match the approved controlled vocabulary entries, computed per document.

primary.description: Residual high-severity violations are reduced by at least 50% in the treatment pipeline compared to baseline for high-risk workloads (w1, w2).
primary.statistical_test: two-sided Mann–Whitney U or permutation test over per-document violation counts; alpha = 0.05

primary.description: PII leakage to external MT/LLM services is effectively eliminated in treatment for high-PII workloads (w3), with no more than 1% of documents leaking any unredacted PII/PHI.

secondary.description: Average pipeline latency increase is no more than 20% in treatment compared to baseline across all workloads.
Terminology compliance improves by at least 20 percentage points for regulated terms in high-risk workloads.
False positive issue rate remains below 0.3 for high-risk workloads, to ensure legal teams are not overwhelmed by spurious flags.
Average legal review time per document does not increase by more than 10% in treatment for high-risk workloads, and ideally decreases due to better triage.

success_criteria.interpretation_notes: If primary criteria are met but latency or false positives exceed targets, the design may still be acceptable for highest-risk content but not for lower-risk pipelines; results should be stratified by workload and risk profile.

failure_modes.name: ruleset_overfitting_or_gaps
failure_modes.description: Rule-based checks are too narrow or too broad, either missing common violation patterns or triggering on benign patterns; this manifests as high residual violation rate or high false positive rate.
failure_modes.detection: Discrepancy between automated detection metrics and human-annotated violation outcomes; clusters of false positive rules visible in rule-level metrics.

failure_modes.name: ml_model_misclassification
failure_modes.description: Topic/risk classifiers fail to correctly identify high-risk content or hallucinate risk where there is none, leading to misrouted reviews.
failure_modes.detection: Confusion matrices between ML output and human labels on a stratified sample; misclassification particularly around borderline cases (e.g., educational vs. promotional content).

failure_modes.name: pii_redaction_incompleteness_or_overreach
failure_modes.description: PII redaction misses some sensitive entities (increasing leakage risk) or redacts too aggressively, harming translation quality or interpretability.
failure_modes.detection: Residual PII leakage metrics > target; reviewer feedback indicating that crucial non-PII content is masked; manual spot checks on samples with known PII.

failure_modes.name: pipeline_latency_regression
failure_modes.description: Compliance screening stages add excessive latency beyond the 20% budget, making the treatment pipeline operationally unacceptable for time-sensitive workloads.
failure_modes.detection: average_pipeline_latency metric breaching target, with profiling showing hotspots in certain models or rule engines.

failure_modes.name: audit_log_unusability
failure_modes.description: Audit logs are too verbose, inconsistent, or poorly structured to be usable as evidence for regulators or internal auditors.
failure_modes.detection: Manual inspection of generated 'compliance dossiers' reveals missing context, unlinked rules, or inability to trace from a final artifact back to checks and approvals.

failure_modes.name: legal_team_overload
failure_modes.description: Increased number of automated flags leads to significant increase in legal review time and frustration, even if technical metrics look improved.
failure_modes.detection: legal_review_time_per_document and legal_escalation_rate increase substantially; qualitative feedback from reviewers indicates alert fatigue.

runtime.language: Python 3.11 (or later, pinned in requirements.txt / pyproject.toml)
runtime.os: Linux (e.g., Ubuntu 22.04) recommended; macOS supported for local runs; Windows via WSL2
runtime.containerization: Docker with a reproducible image (e.g., Dockerfile in /experiments/ch09-compliance) pinning system and Python dependencies

nlp: spaCy (with appropriate language models for en, es, de, fr) for rule-based NER and tokenization
HuggingFace Transformers + tokenizers for ML classifiers and PII detectors
sentencepiece or similar if underlying MT models require it
ml: scikit-learn or equivalent for evaluation utilities
PyTorch or TensorFlow (pinned versions) for classifier/NER models if not using API-based services
workflow: pydantic or dataclasses for typed configuration
Typer or Click for CLI orchestration
Prefect, Airflow, or a lightweight in-code orchestrator (depending on repository conventions)
logging: structlog or Python logging with JSON formatter for audit logs
sqlite or PostgreSQL (optional) as a backend for storing structured compliance events

external_services.mt_llm: Either (a) a local MT/LLM model served via an internal endpoint, or (b) external API (e.g., Azure OpenAI, Google Cloud Translate) with API keys supplied via environment variables. The experiment code should treat MT/LLM as an abstract interface defined elsewhere in the repo.
external_services.storage: File-based storage for input/output (.jsonl or .csv) plus a directory or bucket for logs (`artifacts/experiments/ch09-compliance`).
external_services.secrets: API keys and database credentials supplied via environment variables or a .env file not committed to version control.

datasets.location: Repository path such as `data/ch09_compliance/` with subdirectories `w1_pharma_ifus`, `w2_financial_disclosures`, `w3_support_tickets_pii`, `w4_lowrisk_marketing`.
datasets.format: Each workload stored as JSONL with fields: `id`, `source_text`, `source_lang`, `target_lang`, `workload_id`, `risk_profile`, `jurisdiction`.

reproducibility.random_seeds: Global random, NumPy, and PyTorch seeds set in a shared utility to a fixed integer (e.g., 90909).
reproducibility.config_files: YAML/JSON config files specifying rule sets, model checkpoints, and thresholds under `configs/ch09_compliance/`.
reproducibility.version_pinning: requirements.txt or lock file committed; Docker image version tagged with experiment_id.

run_instructions.overview: The experiment compares a baseline pipeline with minimal compliance automation to a treatment pipeline embedding pre- and post-localization rule-based and ML-driven compliance checks, redaction, and audit logging. Both operate over identical workloads, with random assignment at document level. Outputs are then sampled for blinded human compliance annotation.
steps: 1. Clone repository and set up environment
- `git clone https://github.com/bookauthority/ai-localization-quality-culture-compliance.git`
- `cd ai-localization-quality-culture-compliance`
- Ensure Docker is installed, or create a Python virtual environment if running without Docker.
- If using Docker: `docker build -f experiments/ch09-compliance/Dockerfile -t ch09-compliance:latest .`
2. Configure credentials and environment variables
- Copy `.env.example` from `experiments/ch09-compliance/` to `.env` and fill in MT/LLM API keys or local endpoint URLs, if required.
- Set any database or storage paths if using DB-backed logging.
3. Prepare datasets
- Verify datasets exist under `data/ch09_compliance/` as specified in required_environment.
- If synthetic data generation scripts are provided (e.g., `scripts/ch09_generate_synthetic_data.py`), run them once to create demo workloads.
4. Generate experimental assignment
- Run `python experiments/ch09-compliance/assign_documents.py --config configs/ch09_compliance/assignment.yaml --seed 90909`.
- This writes a JSONL or CSV file mapping each document ID to `arm` in `{baseline, treatment}` while preserving stratification by workload and risk.
5. Run the baseline pipeline
- Run `python experiments/ch09-compliance/run_pipeline.py --config configs/ch09_compliance/baseline.yaml --assignment artifacts/ch09_compliance/assignment.jsonl --arm baseline`.
- This executes ingestion, localization, basic QA, export, and minimal logging.
- Outputs are written to `artifacts/ch09_compliance/baseline/outputs/` with a per-document JSON containing `source_text`, `translated_text`, and metadata.
6. Run the treatment pipeline
- Run `python experiments/ch09-compliance/run_pipeline.py --config configs/ch09_compliance/treatment.yaml --assignment artifacts/ch09_compliance/assignment.jsonl --arm treatment`.
- This executes ingestion, pre-screening (redaction), pre-compliance checks, localization, post-compliance checks, and audit logging.
- Outputs are written to `artifacts/ch09_compliance/treatment/outputs/` and compliance logs to `artifacts/ch09_compliance/treatment/logs/`.
7. Collect runtime metrics

- Both pipeline runs log per-document timings; aggregate these by running `python experiments/ch09-compliance/aggregate_runtime_metrics.py --input artifacts/ch09_compliance/ --output artifacts/ch09_compliance/runtime_summary.json`.
8. Sample documents for human annotation

- Use the sampling utility: `python experiments/ch09-compliance/sample_for_annotation.py --config configs/ch09_compliance/sampling.yaml --outputs-dir artifacts/ch09_compliance/ --output artifacts/ch09_compliance/human_annotation_batches/`.
- This creates blinded annotation files for reviewers with no indication of baseline vs. treatment.
9. Conduct human compliance annotation
- Provide annotators with annotation guidelines (e.g., `docs/ch09_compliance_guidelines.md`).
- Collect completed annotations as JSONL with fields: `doc_id`, `arm_blinded`, `workload_id`, `violations`: [ { `severity`, `category`, `description` } ], `annotation_time_minutes`.
10. Evaluate experiment outcomes

- Run `python experiments/ch09-compliance/evaluate.py --annotations artifacts/ch09_compliance/human_annotations/ --logs artifacts/ch09_compliance/ --output artifacts/ch09_compliance/eval_results.json`.
- This script computes metrics defined in `metrics`, stratified by workload and arm, and (optionally) runs simple statistical tests.
11. Review audit logs and dossiers

- Generate per-artifact compliance dossiers with `python experiments/ch09-compliance/generate_dossiers.py --logs artifacts/ch09_compliance/treatment/logs/ --outputs artifacts/ch09_compliance/treatment/outputs/ --output-dir artifacts/ch09_compliance/treatment/dossiers/`.
- Manually inspect a subset to assess quality as potential regulator-facing evidence.
12. Archive experiment configuration
- Save the exact configs, code commit hash, and environment metadata into `artifacts/ch09_compliance/manifest.json` for reproducibility.
run_instructions.notes: All metric computations should be deterministic given fixed inputs and seeds. Any change to rules, models, or risk thresholds requires a new experiment_id or a clearly versioned configuration file.

fields.doc_id: string, unique identifier for each document
fields.workload_id: string, one of {w1-pharma-ifus, w2-financial-disclosures, w3-support-tickets-pii, w4-lowrisk-marketing}
fields.source_text_hash: string, hash (e.g., SHA-256) of normalized source text
fields.target_text_hash: string, hash of final localized text
fields.pii_present_in_source: boolean or categorical flag based on automated detection
fields.pii_sent_to_external: boolean, indicates if any unredacted PII/PHI was included in text sent to MT/LLM
fields.pii_present_in_output: boolean, indicates if PII/PHI is present in final output

auto_issues.rule_or_model_id: string, identifier of rule or ML model
auto_issues.span: optional text span or character offsets

terminology_compliance.required_terms: integer, count of required regulated terms expected
terminology_compliance.noncompliant_terms: integer, count of terms not matching controlled vocabulary
terminology_compliance.compliance_rate: float, 1 - noncompliant_terms/required_terms (or null if not applicable)

timings.start_time_utc: ISO 8601 timestamp when pipeline started for this doc
timings.legal_review_time_minutes: float or null if not reviewed

legal_outcome.approved: boolean or null if not reviewed

audit_trail_reference.log_file: string, path to raw log file
audit_trail_reference.dossier_file: string, path to compiled compliance dossier for this doc

fields.n_documents: integer, number of documents in this aggregation

config_snapshot.ruleset_versions: mapping from ruleset name to version/tag
config_snapshot.model_versions: mapping from model name to version/checkpoint
